title: Regularity of a locally Noetherian scheme tested at closed points
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Then $X$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] if and only if, for every closed point $x\in X$ (meaning $\{x\}$ is closed in the underlying topological space), the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a regular local ring. The empty scheme is allowed.

proof.text: Assume $X$ is regular and let $x\in X$ be a closed point. By the defining condition of [def-weil-regular-scheme], $x$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U$ with $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$ Noetherian and regular. Let $\mathfrak p_x\subset R$ be the prime of $x$. Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] gives a ring isomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p_x}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Since $R$ is a regular ring, $R_{\mathfrak p_x}$ is a regular local ring by the definition of a regular ring in [def-weil-regular-scheme]. A ring isomorphism identifies the unique maximal ideals and their generating sets, preserves Noetherianity and Krull dimension, so $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a regular local ring. This proves the forward implication. The step uses only the defining affine-open condition, not the stalkwise reformulation stated in the definition, and not the criterion being proved.

Conversely assume the local rings at all closed points of $X$ are regular local, and fix any $x\in X$. Apply [lem-per-locally-noetherian-closed-specialization] to the given locally Noetherian scheme to obtain $c\in\overline{\{x\}}$ with $\{c\}$ closed in $X$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,c}$. The hypothesis therefore makes $A$ a regular local ring. No quasi-compactness of $X$ or Jacobson hypothesis is needed.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] with $Y=X$, $y=c$ and $A=\mathcal O_{X,c}$. Its clause (1) says that the image of $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ consists of all generalizations of $c$. Since $c\in\overline{\{x\}}$, choose $q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $a(q)=x$. Clause (2) identifies $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A,q}$. Apply clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] to the entire affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose global sections are $A$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Writing $\mathfrak q$ for the prime corresponding to $q$, it identifies the latter stalk with $A_{\mathfrak q}$. Hence $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong A_{\mathfrak q}$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], applied to the regular local ring $A$ from Step 2 and the prime $\mathfrak q$ from Step 3, $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local. Transport this property along the ring isomorphism in Step 3 to obtain regularity of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. A ring isomorphism identifies the unique maximal ideals, their generating sets and prime chains, and preserves Noetherianity. So it preserves the defining equality for a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Since $x$ was arbitrary, every stalk $\mathcal O_{X,y}$, $y\in X$, is regular local. Now verify the defining condition of [def-weil-regular-scheme] at an arbitrary $y\in X$. By [pqf-def-locnoeth] there is an affine open $U\ni y$ in the given covering with $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$ Noetherian. Let $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ be the open immersion with image $U$. For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, put $z=\iota_U(\mathfrak p)\in U$, so $\mathfrak p_z=\mathfrak p$ by injectivity. Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] gives $R_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{X,z}$, and the latter is regular local by what was just shown, so $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local by the same transport. Hence the Noetherian ring $R$ is regular, and $U$ is the required affine open neighbourhood of $y$. Thus $X$ is regular. If $X$ is empty, the condition is vacuous.
